Subject: Eval gating for promptset v3 + rollout questions

Hi team,

Following up from the product sync: Acme has offered to pilot our promptset v3 candidate (attached) in a small A/B against their current integration. Before we sign off to run a canary with production traffic, I need alignment on a few cross-functional items so we don't ship and then scramble on regressions.

High-level asks:
- Product: what are the hard acceptance thresholds for A/B (perplexity/GOAL recall/quality score)? Do we require statistical significance or a fixed delta?
- SRE/Runtime: acceptable tail-latency impact (p95/p99) if we enable the new caching behavior for v3?
- Eval/Quality: what minimum pass rate on the regression prompt set triggers a block (and do we run pairwise tests on categories)?
- Sales/CS: timeline constraints for Acme pilot (target start date Feb 21).

I attached a simple A/B plan (eval-plan-abmatrix.xlsx) and the promptset candidate. My proposed guardrail is: if any critical category (PHI redaction, policy-sensitive hallucination, numeric-answer stability) drops below 92% pass on our regression set OR any customer-facing quality metric drops by >3% absolute, we do not proceed to canary. But I want product to confirm.

Can everyone reply with the single-line answer for their area + any blockers by EOD Friday? If needed, we can pull a 30m follow-up.

Thanks,
Dev

--
Dev Patel
Program Manager, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Eval gating for promptset v3 + rollout questions

Thanks Dev — good summary. Quick answers inline: 

- Product acceptance thresholds: we want both statistical significance and a minimum absolute delta. Specifically: 95% confidence (two-sided) and an absolute improvement >= 2% on our composite quality score (weighed across fluency, accuracy, and instruction-following). For regressions, any drop >= 1.5% on the composite quality score is actionable; >=3% triggers an automatic hold.

- Regarding categories: we will require per-category checks for the three critical categories you listed. For each critical category the pass threshold is 92% as you suggested.

- Timeline: Feb 21 start is plausible from product side if Ops finalizes rollout policy by Feb 18.

Notes/requests: please add the composite scoring rubric to the Drive doc (I dropped a template). Also, Markus — can you confirm whether the runtime change for prefix caching is toggleable per-customer? If so, we can cross the latency risk by enabling the old path for Acme if needed.

Happy to take a 30m to finalize if others prefer.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: Eval gating for promptset v3 + rollout questions

Laura (and team),

Short answer: yes — the caching behavior is toggleable at customer scope. A few implementation caveats:
- Toggle is available in the Dedicated/Private paths today; for hosted API it's a runtime flag we can expose for a single customer but there is a small risk window while the flag is propagating (~30m).
- Enabling the new kv-prefix cache increases p95 token latencies by ~12% in our internal perf tests on T4-equivalent hardware for long context prompts; p99 moves ~8% on long tails. Short contexts (<512 tokens) see <5% change.

Recommendation: run the pilot with caching disabled for Acme if they are latency-sensitive (they indicated some 3rd-party fuzzing that requires stable tails). If throughput cost matters we can flip caching on for a daytime window after initial validation.

I attached the quick perf table in the Drive link.

-Markus

Thanks all — here are the Eval/Quality confirmations and the plan I propose: 

1) Regression rule set:
- Run the full regression prompt set (attached: regression-sample-prompts.txt) plus the customer prompt sample (Acme provided ~120 queries).
- Compute composite quality score (weights: accuracy 50, instruction-following 30, hallucination/robustness 20) per-run.
- Accept if: composite score improves >=2% & no critical category drops below 92%.
- If composite score drops between 1%–2% we require root-cause triage and a targeted promptset tweak; any drop >=3% -> block.

2) A/B plan and statistical approach:
- We will use a one-sided test for lift detection in the pilot (because Acme wants to see improvement) but regressions will be treated as two-sided for blocking decisions.
- Minimum sample: 1,200 impressions per variant to reach 95% power for small effect sizes (2% delta) on the composite score. If Acme cannot provide that in 7 days, extend to 14 days or reduce per-variant sensitivity.

3) Rollout guardrails and exception flow:
- If any blocking condition occurs, immediate rollback and open an incident with Engineering + Product + Eval.
- For non-blocking but concerning degradation (e.g., 1.5% drop), open a follow-up CR with target fixes; a second pilot will be required.

Action items: Dev — please confirm that Acme can provide the 1,200 impressions/variant baseline and attach any example logs they will send. Emily, can you confirm sampling availability and whether we should limit to specific endpoints/paths?

If all good, I will publish the final eval checklist to the Drive doc and kick off the experiment runbook.

Thanks,
Soojin
